# Results — Study 92 (Easy-Money) on the real tapes

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — document the
**decay of the long-vol ETP VIXY** (total-return adjusted, so its several **1:4 reverse
splits** are folded into one continuous NAV), then **short it 1×** to harvest the contango
carry, net of **5 bps** one-way trade cost and **300 bps/yr** stock borrow (shorts pay
borrow, daily), acting one day after sizing (signal at close *t* → return at *t+1*). We
report the headline Sharpe AND the **tail** it hides — skew, excess kurtosis, worst day,
max drawdown — then the **leverage that survives the worst day**. As-of **2026-06-12**;
window is **VIXY-bounded (2011+)**. Match the fingerprints to confirm you hold the same tapes.*

## Data stamp

| Series | Window | Rows | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| VIXY (total return, long-vol ETP) | 2011-01-04 → 2026-06-12 | 3,883 | `929eac2a9e69` |
| ^VIX (spot index, context) | 1990-01-02 → 2026-06-12 | 9,180 | `5d2cac5c3812` |

> Note: `quantlab` flags VIXY's **2024-08-05 +43%** day as ">±40%". It is a *genuine*
> market event (the yen carry-unwind; spot VIX jumped 23→39 that day), not an adjustment
> artefact — it is the single worst day for the short-vol book and is kept, not scrubbed.

## (1) The carry is real and large — VIXY just bleeds

| Metric | Value |
|---|--:|
| Total return over the window | **−100.0%** (ends at **0.0037%** of its starting NAV) |
| CAGR | **−48.46%/yr** |
| Annualised vol | 69.9% |
| Worst day / best day | −20.9% / **+43.1%** |

A dollar in VIXY at launch is worth about **0.0037 cents** today. The contango roll-decay
is one of the most reliable large negative drifts in any liquid security — the carry a
short would collect is unambiguously real.

## (2) The short-vol carry — net of 5 bps/turn + 300 bps/yr borrow, 1× capital

| Metric | Value |
|---|--:|
| CAGR | **+14.79%/yr** |
| Annualised vol | 69.9% |
| **Sharpe** | **0.568** |
| **HAC *t* on the daily return** | **+2.31** |
| Max drawdown | **−92.3%** |
| Skewness | **−1.66** |
| Excess kurtosis | **+9.4** |
| Worst single day | **−43.1%** (the 2024-08-05 spike) |
| Final equity | 8.38× start |

The carry **earns** — and the HAC *t* clears the bar (**+2.31 > 2**), so the Signal is
`REAL` on this tape. But the Sharpe of **0.568** is the headline that lies: the payoff is
**left-skewed (−1.66)** with **fat tails (excess kurtosis +9.4)**, a worst day of **−43%**
and a **−92% drawdown**. That is the textbook signature of *selling insurance*, not free
money — a steady drip punctuated by catastrophe (Feb 2018 Volmageddon, Mar 2020 COVID,
Aug 2024). XIV, the inverse ETN, did not survive its drawdown in 2018.

## (3) Sizing that survives the tail kills the return

| Metric | Value |
|---|--:|
| Survivable leverage (worst day ≤ 25% of capital) | **0.581×** |
| CAGR at that size | +15.67%/yr |
| Sharpe at that size | **0.568** (unchanged — linear scaling) |
| Max drawdown at that size | **−72.0%** |

Even shrinking the position so the **worst historical day** costs at most a quarter of
capital, the strategy still draws down **−72%**, and the Sharpe is the same **0.568** —
because de-levering a single-asset short cannot change its Sharpe, only its scale. You
cannot diversify away a one-day −43% move in the underlying; you can only hold less of it,
and holding less of it scales the steady carry down in lock-step. There is no size at
which this is "easy money."

## The decisive numbers

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Is the contango carry real? | **Yes** — VIXY's CAGR is **−48.46%/yr**; shorting it earns **+14.79%/yr**, HAC *t* **+2.31**. |
| Is it *free / easy* money? | **No** — skew **−1.66**, excess kurtosis **+9.4**, worst day **−43%**, max drawdown **−92%**. |
| Can strict sizing rescue it? | **Not really** — sized to survive the worst day (0.58×) it still draws down **−72%** at the same Sharpe. |
| What is it, then? | A **compensated risk premium** — you are short crash insurance, paid a steady drip to pay out in vol spikes. |

## How to read it

- **Signal → REAL.** The carry is genuine and statistically certified on the real tape
  (HAC *t* = +2.31). VIXY's relentless −48%/yr decay is the carry, and shorting it banks
  a positive, autocorrelation-robust mean return.
- **Free money? → BUSTED** (3rd axis). The Sharpe is a mirage of safety: a −1.66-skewed,
  +9.4-excess-kurtosis payoff with a −92% drawdown and a −43% worst day is **selling
  insurance**, not a free coupon. The premium is the price of the crashes you eventually
  pay for (Feb 2018 took XIV to zero).
- **Tradability → FRAGILE.** The edge survives costs and borrow, and is investable *only*
  at a tiny, tail-disciplined size — at which the absolute return is small and the
  drawdown still −72%. One mis-sized spike (the leverage XIV ran) is terminal. Tradable in
  principle, fragile in practice.

python examples/verify.py             # real tapes (this doc)
